assessment.nobel_worthiness: Elucidation of GLP-1 as an incretin and its conversion into long-acting receptor agonists has produced a new class of drugs that transformed type 2 diabetes care and obesity treatment, with cardiovascular and renal benefits now documented. A rare combination of basic physiology, peptide chemistry and very large clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: Decisive work is distributed: Drucker (intestinotrophic and physiological actions, translation), Holst (human physiology of GLP-1 secretion and action), Mojsov (identification of the bioactive GLP-1 peptide form and its synthesis). Habener and others are not on the supplied credit list, and Knudsen's role was largely industrial drug development; the three-person ceiling forces a hard choice that remains contested.
assessment.maturity: Therapeutic efficacy is confirmed in multiple large independent trials across many agents over more than a decade; the physiology is stable. Recognition is timely, arguably overdue given the scale of clinical use.
uncertainties: Priority and credit between academic discoverers and industrial developers is disputed.
Long-term safety and durability of effect on obesity outcomes are still being accumulated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells with chimeric antigen receptors have produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell leukemias and lymphomas and have established a new therapeutic modality (living drugs). Originality in receptor design with costimulation is high and the clinical impact is clear.
assessment.attribution: June (clinical translation of CD19 CAR-T with 4-1BB, first durable responses in CLL), Sadelain (CD28 costimulation and early design of second-generation CARs), Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer and early gene-engineered T-cell trials) form a plausible trio. Eshhar's original chimeric-receptor concept and others are not in the supplied credit list, so the original-concept share is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and over a decade of follow-up confirm durable benefit in hematologic malignancies. Solid-tumor efficacy and safety (cytokine release, secondary malignancy signals) remain open, but the core discovery is mature.
uncertainties: Credit for the original chimeric receptor concept versus clinical realization.
Limited efficacy in solid tumors and long-term safety signals.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new intracellular signaling pathway from the endoplasmic reticulum to the nucleus, revealing how cells sense and adapt to protein-folding stress. It is conceptually original, mechanistically complete (IRE1, XBP1 splicing, HAC1, and downstream branches) and underlies understanding of diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori independently and complementarily defined the core IRE1/HAC1 and the ATF6 branches respectively; the two-person configuration is clean. Ron and Harding on PERK are plausible additional contributors but are outside the supplied credit list.
assessment.maturity: Thirty years of confirmation across yeast, mammals and disease models; the framework is textbook. Therapeutic exploitation is still emerging, but Nobel-style fundamental recognition is mature.
uncertainties: Direct clinical translation is limited so far.
Relative contribution of the PERK branch is not represented in the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational targeting of the BCR-ABL kinase with imatinib turned chronic myeloid leukemia from a fatal into a largely chronic disease and established the paradigm of molecularly targeted cancer therapy. Impact is major and unambiguous.
assessment.attribution: Druker (clinical development and proof of concept), Lydon (the medicinal programme and kinase-inhibitor concept at Ciba-Geigy), Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) are the standard trio. Rowley, Witte, Konopka and others on the BCR-ABL discovery are outside the supplied credit; the biological discovery of the target was recognized only partly.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of follow-up and universal confirmation across the kinase-inhibitor field; recognition is mature and arguably late.
uncertainties: Allocation between the target's biological discovery and the drug development is unresolved.
Industrial versus academic credit for Lydon.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Demonstrating that TNF is a dominant driver in rheumatoid arthritis and that its blockade is effective established cytokine-targeted therapy and benefited many inflammatory diseases, a paradigm shift in autoimmune disease treatment.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini jointly carried out the mechanistic work and the first clinical trials; the two-person configuration is clean and widely accepted. Contributions by Vilcek, Cerami, and Kollias on TNF biology are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Over twenty years of confirmation, with multiple approved anti-TNF agents and extensive real-world evidence. Recognition is mature; the field has many antecedents so priority may be debated.
uncertainties: Role of other TNF pioneers and antibody engineers is not represented in the credit list.
Biologic therapy is not curative and has been partly displaced by newer drug classes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle vaccines against HPV prevent infection and are producing large reductions in cervical precancer and cancer, a rare case of cancer prevention by vaccination. Clear, original solution to a specific problem with large public-health consequence.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (L1 VLP self-assembly and immunogenicity), Frazer (early VLP work and expression strategies) are credited; the credit is usually divided with Zhou (Frazer's collaborator, deceased) and with industrial groups. The proposed trio is plausible but the allocation of the VLP priority is contested.
assessment.maturity: Population-level data from multiple countries now show strong reductions in cervical precancer and cancer; recognition is timely, especially as zur Hausen's HPV discovery was recognized in 2008.
uncertainties: Priority dispute between groups that independently produced VLPs.
Complete cancer-incidence benefit is still emerging in the earliest vaccinated cohorts.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Adult stem-cell derived organoids are self-organizing three-dimensional cultures from single Lgr5-positive stem cells that provide a general platform for modelling tissue biology, cancer and infection and for personalized therapy testing. Originality and breadth of adoption are high.
assessment.attribution: Clevers (Lgr5 stem cells and organoid concept) and Sato (first intestinal organoid culture) form a natural two-person attribution. Others such as Kuo and Bissell contributed related 3D culture concepts but are outside the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Fast adoption and independent replication across tissues, but clinical impact is still developing and relative to earlier recognized stem-cell work the timing may be early.
uncertainties: Clinical benefit of organoid-guided therapy is not yet firmly established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense modulation of SMN2 splicing (nusinersen) led to the first effective therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, changing a fatal infant disease and validating splice-switching oligonucleotides as a drug modality. Mechanistic clarity and clinical effect are strong.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (mechanism and identification of the ISS-N1 / splicing-regulatory target) and Bennett (antisense chemistry and drug development) are complementary and form a fair pair. Others, such as Singh and Hua, contributed significantly but are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Controlled trials and years of real-world follow-up confirm benefit, with later SMA therapies strengthening the picture. Recognition is plausibly timely, though a longer track record would reinforce it.
uncertainties: Credit among academic and industrial co-developers is contestable.
Long-term durability and interaction with gene therapy approaches remain to be defined.
